structured_output.analysis: There is almost no spare budget: the best grid uses 3.1480 bits against 3.1484. Any upgrade has to be paid for. The retrieved records only give KL for the layers that lose the most, so a cheap downgrade can't be picked from data. Three ways to make room: 1) Change only options, which costs no bits: act_order=True for every GPTQ method. 2) Use group_size=256 for the 109 rht_gptq_int3 layers. This frees roughly 0.07 bits per weight in scale overhead, and the rotation should make larger groups hurt less. The freed bits pay for one bit-width step up on the 4 layers with the biggest measured single-layer gains: 14.down from rht_gptq_int2 to rht_gptq_int3 (0.00633 to 0.00181), 27.gate from rht_gptq_int3 to rht_gptq_int4 (0.00499 to 0.00153), 27.up from gptq_int3 to gptq_int4 (0.00572 to 0.00217) and 2.up from gptq_int3 to gptq_int4 (0.00642 to 0.00237). 3) The same group trade with a different set of upgrades.

proposals.name: actorder_all
proposals.rationale: No bits change, only options: act_order=True on every GPTQ method, starting from iso_3.15 (measured KL 0.43614 [E514ab09c524e]). GPTQ layers at 3 and 2 bits carry the largest losses, e.g. 27.up gptq_int3 0.00572 [Ef04d8aa7bded] and 14.down rht_gptq_int2 0.00633 [E4c3f9b73e065]. 27.up also has weight kurtosis 10.41 [Ee42a8c6e7545].

proposals.name: g256rht3_up4
proposals.rationale: Setting weight.group_size=256 on rht_gptq_int3 pays for 4 upgrades with the largest measured single-layer gains. 14.down: rht_gptq_int2 0.00633 [E4c3f9b73e065] to rht_gptq_int3 0.00181 [E90bd4b2f3645]. 27.gate: rht_gptq_int3 0.00499 [Efa0bb391da67] to rht_gptq_int4 0.00153 [Ef428ac081334]. 27.up: gptq_int3 0.00572 [Ef04d8aa7bded] to gptq_int4 0.00217 [Efea8c18d2abc]. 2.up: gptq_int3 0.00642 [E9baa10763ebe] to gptq_int4 0.00237 [Ef3d9c7b4502c]. Base is iso_3.15, KL 0.43614 [E514ab09c524e].
